# 1 Enoch Chapter 106 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Birth of Noah (Appendix)

---

**106:1** And after some days my son Methuselah took a wife for his son Lamech, and she became pregnant by him and bore a son.

**106:2** And his body was white as snow and red as the blooming of a rose, and the hair of his head and his long locks were white as wool, and his eyes were beautiful.

**106:3** And when he opened his eyes, he lit up the whole house like the sun, and the whole house was exceedingly bright.

**106:4** And thereupon he arose in the hands of the midwife, opened his mouth and spoke with the Lord of Righteousness.

**106:5** And his father Lamech was afraid of him and fled, and came to his father Methuselah.

**106:6** And he said to him: "I have begotten a strange son, unlike and different from man, resembling the sons of the God of heaven; and his nature is different and he is not like us, and his eyes are like the rays of the sun, and his countenance is glorious.

**106:7** And it seems to me that he is not sprung from me but from the angels; and I fear that a wonder may be wrought in his days upon the earth.

**106:8** And now, my father, I am here to petition you and implore you to go to Enoch our father and learn the truth from him, for his dwelling place is among the angels."

**106:9** And when Methuselah heard the words of his son, he came to me at the ends of the earth — for he had heard that I was there — and he cried aloud, and I heard his voice and came to him. And I said to him: "Here I am, my son; why have you come to me?"

**106:10** And he answered and said: "Because of a great cause of anxiety have I come to you, and because of a disturbing vision have I approached you.

**106:11** And now, my father, hear me: to Lamech my son there has been born a son, the like of whom there is none, and his nature is not like our nature, and the color of his body is whiter than snow and redder than the bloom of a rose, and the hair of his head is whiter than white wool, and his eyes are like the rays of the sun; and he opened his eyes and at once lit up the whole house.

**106:12** And he arose in the hands of the midwife, and opened his mouth and blessed the Lord of heaven.

**106:13** And his father Lamech was afraid and fled to me, and did not believe that he was sprung from him but that he was in the likeness of the angels of heaven; and behold, I have come to you that you may make known to me the truth."

**106:14** And I, Enoch, answered and said to him: "The Lord will do a new thing on the earth, and this I have already seen in a vision, and I make known to you that in the generation of my father Jared some of the angels of heaven transgressed the word of the Lord.

**106:15** And behold, they commit sin and transgress the law, and have united themselves with women and commit sin with them, and have married some of them, and have begotten children by them.

**106:16** And they shall produce on the earth giants — not according to the spirit but according to the flesh — and there will be great punishment on the earth, and the earth shall be cleansed from all impurity.

**106:17** Yes, there shall come great destruction over the whole earth, and there shall be a flood and great destruction for one year.

**106:18** And this son who has been born to you shall be left on the earth, and his three sons shall be saved with him; when all mankind on the earth shall die, he shall be kept safe.

**106:19** And now make known to your son Lamech that he who has been born is truly his son, and call his name Noah; for he shall be left to you, and he and his sons shall be saved from the destruction that shall come upon the earth on account of all the sin and unrighteousness that shall be completed on the earth in his days."

---

*SOPHIA notes: LOGOS register adopted for the narrative, with PNEUMA's vivid touches preserved where they serve the text. The double retelling (Lamech's report in vv. 6–8, Methuselah's retelling in vv. 10–13) is preserved in full — the repetition is structurally significant, not redundant. V. 4: "spoke with the Lord of Righteousness" (EMET/LOGOS) preferred over "blessed the Lord of heaven" (v. 12, EMET) — the two verses describe the same event differently in different manuscripts; both are translated as presented. The glowing-baby details (vv. 2–3) are preserved exactly. Divergences logged.*
